chapters.title: Chapter 1: Everyday Foundations

grammar.title: The Nominal Sentence (الجُمْلَة الاسْمِيَّة)
grammar.text: Arabic has no verb for 'is' or 'are' in the present tense. Placing a subject next to an attribute completes the sentence: اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ means Allah [is] One; أَنَا جَائِعٌ means I [am] hungry.

sentences.en: How much is the price for this?

chapters.aiScenario: You are a warm Arabic conversation partner. I am a beginner (A1 level). Greet me politely in Arabic and ask how I am. Let's practice ordering food or water and asking where the mosque is. Keep your replies short (under 2 sentences), in Modern Standard Arabic with full vowels, and gently correct mistakes.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Wants, Needs & Requests

sentences.en: I am thirsty, I want tea.
I want a cup of coffee.
Here you go, this is your money.
Thank you, I don't want anything else.

chapters.aiScenario: You are a friendly waiter at an Arab restaurant. Greet me, take my order for food and drinks, ask if I need anything else, and bring me the bill. Keep it strictly A1 Arabic.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Hotel, Taxis & Travel

grammar.title: Having with 'Indi (عِنْدِي)
grammar.text: Arabic expresses possession with the prepositional phrase عِنْدِي (literally 'at me / with me'). عِنْدِي حَجْزٌ = I have a reservation. To negate: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي or مَا عِنْدِي = I do not have.

sentences.en: I have a reservation at the hotel.
Take me to the hotel, please.
This is my luggage in the car.
How much is the fare to there?

chapters.aiScenario: Roleplay: You are a hotel receptionist in Medina. I arrive to check in. Greet me, ask for my reservation and passport, hand me the room key, and answer where the elevator is in simple A1 Arabic.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Time, Routine & Actions

sentences.en: I will go to the lesson tomorrow.
I read the Quran after Fajr.
I have an appointment in the evening.
I wrote a letter to my brother.
I don't know the meaning of this word.
The time now is exactly three o'clock.

chapters.aiScenario: You are my Arabic language tutor having a warm check-in. Ask me what I did today, when I read Quran, and what my plans are for tomorrow. Speak in simple A1 Arabic.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Questions & Meeting People

words: to know you / with your acquaintance

sentences.en: Praise be to Allah, fine and well.
Is it possible you help me?
I am very sorry for being late.

chapters.aiScenario: You are meeting me for the first time at a cafe in Amman. Greet me, ask my name, where I am from, what I do, and how long I have been learning Arabic. Keep sentences under 15 words.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Home & Furniture

grammar.title: Describing Rooms (Adjective Agreement)
grammar.text: Non-human plurals and feminine nouns take feminine singular adjectives: غُرْفَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ (a beautiful room); شُقَقٌ وَاسِعَةٌ (spacious flats).

sentences.en: I live in a beautiful flat.
In the flat is a bedroom and kitchen.
This is the spacious living room.
I have a bed in the bedroom.
In the kitchen is a fridge and a new oven.
Around the dining table are many chairs.
The carpet on the floor is clean.
On which floor do you live?
I live on the third floor.

chapters.aiScenario: Roleplay: You are an apartment owner showing me around a flat in Cairo. Describe the rooms, what furniture is included (bed, oven, fridge), and tell me which floor it is on. Speak simply.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Shopping & The Market

sentences.en: How much is the price of this shirt?
This is cheap and that is expensive.
I want three kilos of this.
Do you have a bigger size?
This is a very excellent thing.
May Allah bless you in your business.

chapters.aiScenario: You are a merchant at the Souq in Jeddah. I want to buy a thobe or dates. Negotiate courteously with me, tell me the price, and accept cash or card.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Conversation Repair Kit

sentences.en: How do I say this in Arabic?
What is the meaning of this word?
I did not understand, repeat please.
I am learning the Arabic language.

chapters.aiScenario: You are my Arabic practice partner. Test my repair phrases by deliberately speaking slightly fast or using a new word, and encourage me to ask you to repeat, speak slowly, or explain the word in Arabic.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: The Mosque & Worship

sentences.en: Where is the place of wudu?
We prayed in congregation in the mosque.
What is the name of the Imam of the Haram?
I want a mushaf to read.
May Allah reward you with the best reward.
I pray to Allah for your success.
Peace and Allah's mercy be upon you.

chapters.aiScenario: We are at the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah. Ask me if I have made wudu, where we should sit to read Quran, and remind me of the time for Asr prayer in simple Arabic.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Days, Weeks & Plans

sentences.en: Tomorrow I have a lesson with the teacher.
How many hours do you study a day?

sentences.ar: أَقْضِي عُطْلَةَ نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي.
sentences.en: I spend the weekend with my family.
sentences.tr: aqḍī ʿuṭlata nihāyati l-usbūʿi maʿa ʿāʾilatī.

sentences.en: In the morning I drink tea.
In the evening I read a book.

chapters.aiScenario: You are an Arabic conversation partner talking about our week. Ask me what day today is, what I did yesterday, and when my next Arabic class is.
